items.q: A market was worth £710m in 2024 and £960m in 2025. What was the percentage change?
items.why: Percentage change = (new – old) ÷ old × 100 = (960 – 710) ÷ 710 × 100 = 35.2%. Divide by the old figure.
items.label: New question

items.q: Actual output = 35,500 units. Maximum output = 46,500 units. Capacity utilisation = ?
items.why: CU = (actual output / maximum output) x 100 = (35,500 / 46,500) x 100 = 76.34%. Simple division: 35,500 / 46,500 = 0.7634 = 76.34%.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: In 2007 a business had sales of £10 million in a market worth £125 million. In 2017 its sales were £12.6 million and its market share was 6%. Calculate the percentage growth in the size of the market between 2007 and 2017.
items.why: Market size in 2017 = £12.6m ÷ 0.06 = £210m. Growth = (£210m – £125m) ÷ £125m × 100 = 68%. 26% is the growth in the business's own sales, not the market.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2018 Q17

items.q: The decision tree shows two options. Which option should be chosen on financial grounds, and what is its net gain?
items.why: Option A: expected value = (0.6 × £20m) + (0.4 × –£1m) = £11.6m. Net gain = £11.6m – £5m = £6.6m. Option B: expected value = (0.25 × £14m) + (0.75 × £0m) = £3.5m. Net gain = £3.5m – £4m = –£0.5m. Option A has the higher net gain. Compare net gains, not expected values.
items.label: New question

items.q: Revenue £69m, cost of sales £40m, operating expenses £10m, net finance costs £3m, taxation £3m. What is the gross profit?
items.why: Gross profit = revenue – cost of sales = £69m – £40m = £29m.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business has revenue of £736,000, cost of sales of £460,000 and payables of £55,000. What are its payables days?
items.why: Payables days = payables ÷ cost of sales × 365 = £55,000 ÷ £460,000 × 365 = 43.6, about 44 days. Payables days use cost of sales, not revenue.
items.label: New question

items.q: A retailer has revenue of £1,215,000, cost of sales of £810,000 and average inventory of £140,000. What is its inventory turnover?
items.why: Inventory turnover = cost of sales ÷ average inventory = £810,000 ÷ £140,000 = 5.8 times a year.
items.label: New question

items.q: Table: Output 0 = £40, 1 = £80, 2 = £110, 3 = £150. Calculate the total variable costs of producing 3 units of output.
items.why: TVC = TC - FC = 150 - 40 = £110. Fixed costs = £40 (costs at zero output). Total costs at 3 units = £150. Same method as Q12. Always start with zero-output row to identify fixed costs, then subtract from total cost.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Marks and Spencer plc, 1 April 2017 (£m): non-current assets 6,569; current assets 1,723; current liabilities 2,368; non-current liabilities 2,774; total equity 3,150. Calculate its gearing.
items.why: Capital employed = total equity + non-current liabilities = 3,150 + 2,774 = 5,924. Gearing = 2,774 ÷ 5,924 × 100 = 46.83%.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2018 Q01.3
